To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the CAK subunit is a component of the TFIIH transcription/DNA repair complex, and that CAK activity is altered upon association within TFIIH.
the CAK complex is a part of TFIII, and the association of CAK within TFIIH alters the substrate specificity of CAK.
the CAK subunits of TF IIH are associated with the XPB and X PD subunits of TF I IH, and that the CAK complex of TFIIH has a substrate specificity that is distinct from that of free CAK and rCAK.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the CAK complex as an integral subcomplex of TFIIH and the effect of this association on the substrate specificity of CAK.
a novel function of TFIIH: it is involved in the regulation of the CAK substrate specificity.
the role of CAK in TFIIH and its function in transcription and DNA repair.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the CAK activity is modulated upon integration into TFIIH.
the substrate specificity of CAK is altered upon association within the TFIIH complex, and that CAK is an integral subcomplex of TFIIH.
CAK is an intrinsic part of the TFIIH complex and that the substrate specificity of the CAK subunit is modulated by its interaction with the other subunits of TFiiH.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the substrate specificity of CAK is altered when it becomes part of TFIIK.
the substrate specificity of the CAK complex is altered upon association to TFIIH.
the CAK subunit is an intrinsic part of TFIII, but that its activity is regulated by association with other TFIIH subcomplexes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CAK is a versatile kinase, able to phosphorylate different substrates depending on whether it is part of a free CAK complex or of TFIIH.
TFIIH is composed of two distinct subcomplexes that are not stably associated with each other and are regulated by the presence of free and bound CAK.
CAK, when associated with the core of TFIIH and in the presence of XPD and XPB, exhibits a substrate specificity that is altered from that of free CAK, which preferentially phosphorylates cdk2.
